newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends marginally down, gilts steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends marginally down, gilts steady.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday in the 7.5-8.0 percent range, down from opening quotes of around 8.5 percent, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trade was done around 8.0-8.5 with stray deals at 8.75 percent.
Call money ended Tuesday around 4.25 percent but a repo auction later in the evening drained 41 billion rupees from banks and pushed rates up on Wednesday.

"We have to see what happens tomorrow," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "With the reporting Friday coming up, rates should ease but with a strike scheduled for July 4, rates may remain at today's levels."
Prices of government securities were largely steady in moderate trade with some stocks showing a rise, dealers said.
"Trade remains cautious as call money has tightened but volumes were better than yesterday," said a dealer. "The market is still waiting to see whether a fresh issue of bonds is in the offing."
He said there was speculation among market players that the government will make a bond issue in the near future as liquidity with banks was good.
Among actively traded stocks, the the 12.59 percent 2004 stock was trade on Wednesday at prices between 100.6 rupees and 100.7 against Tuesday's 102.62, dealers said.
The 12.14 percent 2000 rose to 102 rupees from 101.98, the 13.62 percent 1998 to 104.42 from 104.4 while the 12.69 percent 2002 fell to 102.35 from 102.4, dealers said.
Treasury bills maturing in September 1998 were traded at yields between 8.8 percvent and 8.85 percent, they said.
